captions.text: When you delete a file, your computer usually doesn't !erase it.!
It just marks the space as *free.*
the data stays until something new !overwrites it.!
!SSDs are different.! The computer sends a *TRIM* command,
captions.say: S S Ds are different. The computer sends a trim command,

captions.text: and the drive *clears those blocks* in the background, usually soon after.
So on a modern laptop, deleted often *really means gone.*
On an old hard drive, it means !"not yet".!
